S10281800108d.topic: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh roughly a billion tonnes on Earth.
S10281800108d.title: A Teaspoon of Neutron Star Weighs a Billion Tonnes #shorts
S10281800108d.description:
A neutron star is the collapsed core of a massive star. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tonnes on Earth. Follow for more weird science, explained calmly.

Narration uses an AI voice; visuals are AI-generated illustrations and royalty-free stock. Scripts are fact-checked, but if you spot a mistake, tell us in the comments.
S10281800108d.narration: A teaspoon of neutron star weighs about a billion tonnes. Let's unpack that. A neutron star is what's left when a massive star runs out of fuel and collapses. Its core crushes down until protons and electrons are squeezed into neutrons. Now picture about one and a half times the Sun's mass. Packed into a ball roughly 20 kilometers across. Roughly the size of a city. Your teaspoon of sugar weighs about five grams. This one weighs about two and a half times as much as all the people on Earth combined. Mount Everest, by comparison, is roughly 160 times heavier than that teaspoon. Some neutron stars spin hundreds of times a second. Wait, it gets weirder: they can sweep beams of radio waves like lighthouses. It's just matter squeezed beyond anything on Earth. Mind-bending, right? Follow for more weird science.
